original_analysis: Four hypothetical players each have ten distinct sessions with fixed outcomes under a sharp no-treatment-effect hypothesis. Uniformly assigning exactly two players yields six valid assignments, with two absolute differences of 1. Individual-row reassignment admits forbidden split-player allocations.
checks: Source and full-reader review distinguish finite randomization inference from asymptotic cluster methods.
Summarizing player numerators/counts preserves the chosen pooled ratio, not a universal inference fix.
limits: No real player data or online experiment.
Perfect within-player outcome agreement is deliberately assumed; extra sessions can contain useful information in other designs.
Random assignment does not establish unconditional cross-player independence.
No general sample-size, significance, launch or asymptotic-calibration guarantee.
Identity, interference, selection, missingness and stopping conditions require separate checks.
not_performed: Statistical package calibration or game execution

deduplication.scope: Full pinned analyst, completion, retention, ten-success, exposure, stopping and historical-role texts. Not an all-history semantic audit.
deduplication.distinct_value: An explicit admissible assignment space and analysis handoff beyond the existing generic dependence warning.
